also: leave it up to someone to

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: alicui aliquid, or alicui ut (nē) with the subjunctive
evidence: Caes. BG 4.21: Volusēnō mandat, ut … (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 1.10.3: praetereā typōs tibi mandō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From manus and dō, “put into someone’s hand” (Lewis & Short). Not mandō, mandere, to chew.

sources: Lewis & Short: mando
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 102, 338.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
